title: Card Game Writing Canon
body:
# Card Game Writing Canon

This record establishes canonical standards for card game writing content. These standards govern flavor text, rules text, reminder text, and card naming. They take precedence over general-canon for the card-game domain.

---

## Flavor Text Word Count Limits

**Standard flavor text:** 15–30 words. This is a hard constraint, not a guideline. Card text boxes have fixed physical space. Flavor text that exceeds 30 words will be cut in production, potentially mid-sentence. The section-drafter must count words before delivering flavor text.

**Short flavor text:** 8–15 words for cards with long rules text boxes. When a card has more than two lines of rules text, flavor text is compressed to the short range.

**Reminder text:** 8–15 words, always in parentheses. Reminder text explains a keyword ability for newer players. It must be complete, grammatically correct, and accurate to the mechanical definition. If the mechanical definition requires more than 15 words to state correctly, use fewer keywords and explain differently — do not truncate a reminder text that becomes misleading when cut.

**Wordcount violation severity:** HIGH. Over-length flavor text requires rewrite, not editing.

---

## Reminder Text Conventions

Reminder text is always: parenthetical, present tense, written as a complete sentence or clause. It explains the mechanical term it accompanies — it does not add flavor, it does not cite lore, it does not use proper nouns.

**Correct:** *(When this creature enters the battlefield, create a 1/1 white Soldier token.)*
**Incorrect:** *(Seraphel's blessing manifests as soldiers when she arrives.)* — this is flavor, not reminder text
**Incorrect:** *(Creates tokens when entering.)* — incomplete; tense is wrong

Reminder text is required for: new mechanics in a set, complex or conditional keyword abilities, abilities that new players consistently misread. Reminder text is not required for: base game keywords already well-established (flying, haste, trample), reminder text that would be longer than the rules text it clarifies.

---

## Rules Text Formatting

**One effect per line.** Multiple effects are separated by line breaks, not commas within a single block. When a card has triggered ability + static ability + activated ability, each appears on its own line with its own grammatical structure.

**Consistent keyword usage.** Once a keyword is defined in a set (by the rules text of the first card using it), all subsequent cards using that keyword must use identical text. Variation in keyword text (even minor variation) creates rules ambiguity.

**RFC-equivalent for rules text:** Triggered abilities ALWAYS begin with "When" or "Whenever." Activated abilities ALWAYS use the format "[Cost]: [Effect]." Static abilities NEVER use "When" or "Whenever."

---

## Flavor Text Attribution Format

**Quoted flavor text:** Enclosed in quotation marks. Attribution follows the closing quotation mark, separated by an em-dash. Attribution is italicized. Example: *"The gate does not ask where you are going." —Inscription on the Gate of Endings*

**Unquoted flavor prose:** No quotation marks. No attribution. Present tense preferred. Third person. Example: *The gate does not ask. The gate does not answer.*

**Attribution content:** A name, a title, or a description of the source. Never "unknown" or "anonymous" — if no attribution is appropriate, use unquoted prose instead. Attribution should be brief (5 words maximum). Named characters must be established in the world's canon record or be common-noun descriptions ("an old guard," "the last survivor").

---

## Flavor Text Prohibitions

**Mechanical spoilers:** Flavor text must not explain, hint at, or describe the card's mechanical effect. "She strikes twice" on a double strike creature is a mechanical spoiler. "Her blade never rests" on the same creature is not.

**Fourth-wall breaks:** No references to the game, the players, card games as a concept, or the act of playing. Flavor text exists in the world — not observing it.

**Modern anachronisms in fantasy settings:** Contemporary references (modern technology, pop culture, post-industrial imagery) in pre-industrial fantasy settings are prohibited unless the setting explicitly incorporates them.

**Mechanical keyword names in flavor text:** Keywords are game terms, not world terms. "Flying," "trample," "deathtouch" do not exist as words in the world. Exception: if the keyword is named after a world concept ("Aftermath," "Explore"), it may appear in flavor text in its world sense, not its mechanical sense.

---

## The Flavor-Lore Distinction

**Flavor text** (on cards): Evocative, brief, a moment or impression. Implies story rather than stating it. A reader who has never seen the card before should understand the world is real without needing explanation.

**Lore text** (in guides, compendiums, campaign supplements): Explicit worldbuilding. Names, histories, relationships, motivations. Uses the G-TMPL-003 (D&D Lore Template) conventions adapted for card game worlds.

These are different registers. Do not write flavor text as lore text (too long, too explanatory) or lore text as flavor text (too cryptic, too brief to be usable).
